A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same ColorCtrl work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video editing experiments on PIE-Bench and ColorCtrl-Bench, component ablations, and qualitative real-image and instruction-based editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a user study, downstream fine-tuning, additional metrics, quantitative real-image comparisons, and sensitivity tests.

M1.justification: The core attention-map transfer, masked value replacement, and attribute reweighting remain unchanged. B.9 adds an inference variant using fewer structure-preservation timesteps for broader edits; B.1 separately fine-tunes Step1X-Edit-v1.1 on ColorCtrl-generated data.

E1.justification: The original image/video benchmark coverage remains. v3 adds a synthetic paired-image corpus actually used for downstream training, Chinese-instruction evaluation of the fine-tuned editor (B.1), and style, material, texture, and transparency editing demonstrations beyond the original color-editing task (B.9).

E2.justification: v3 adds PnP-Inversion and FlowEdit comparisons on real images (Table 12), plus an original-versus-fine-tuned Step1X-Edit-v1.1 comparison (Figure 10). FlowEdit's unchanged score row moves from v1's video Table 3 to v3's image Table 1, correcting its placement to match both versions' stated exclusion of FlowEdit from video evaluation.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a randomized, blinded study with 24 experts and 34 cases, Y-GCS/Y-GMS structural metrics, and GPT-4o SC/PQ scoring with three sampled frames per video (B.2, B.5). It also adds downstream fine-tuning and quantitative real-image evaluation protocols. The original benchmark's inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original component ablation and failure examples are retained. v3 adds threshold sensitivity tests at epsilon 0, 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 (Figure 14), crowded/overlapping-object and reflection case studies (Figure 13), and before/after fine-tuning evidence testing the usefulness of generated training data (Figure 10). These substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Both versions retain benchmark seed 42. v3 newly reports preference scores with uncertainty terms in Table 7, including 64.71 ± 9.90% for ColorCtrl. It does not define these terms as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals, or explain their calculation.

E6.justification: The original ColorCtrl benchmark and component-ablation values are retained. v3 adds user preferences, four additional image/video metrics, real-image comparisons, and fine-tuning/application findings. For example, the new real-image Table 12 reports Canny-SSIM of 0.7683 for ColorCtrl, 0.6524 for FlowEdit, and 0.6178 for PnP-Inversion; these are newly reported comparisons under that evaluation.

T1.justification: The rendering/editing formulation in Equations (1)–(2), constraints C1–C3, and attention reasoning are retained. The added standard evaluation measures introduce empirical procedures, without new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free color editing, structural/material preservation, word-level control, superior editing consistency, and generalization across image, video, and instruction-based models. The expanded appendix supports these retained headline contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of threshold robustness, synthetic-data utility, and broader editing enabled by weaker preservation. B.5 distinguishes semantic success from perceptual naturalness and extends the CLIP critique to attribute binding. The existing backbone/localization and inversion limitations are retained, moving from v1 B.3 to v3 B.10.

D1.justification: v3 discloses 40,000 generated training pairs and 2,300 H800 GPU-hours, additional metric implementation details, GPT-4o's evaluation access date, and the user-study interface. It also adds LLM/manual-review disclosure and a future code-release commitment. Most inference and baseline implementation details in Appendix A remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds related-work citations including TextCrafter and ConsistEdit, and explicitly associates TextCrafter with DiTCtrl's attention-consistency problem. Additional references support VIEScore, gradient-based assessment, and CLIP limitations. The overall positioning as training-free MM-DiT color editing remains stable.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose, section order, and Appendix A remain close to v1. Changes include local wording and cross-reference edits, expanded appendix organization, and new Ethics, Reproducibility, and LLM Usage statements; the core explanatory narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the dense two-column format with a single-column ICLR layout, extensively resizes and relocates displays, and adds several experimental figures and tables. v1's video Table 3 is split across v3 Tables 3 and 8. Existing qualitative galleries and failure examples are retained and redistributed, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation: B.5 evaluates edit success and perceptual quality separately, addressing v1's reliance on CLIP scores and qualitative explanations, while B.6 adds quantitative real-image evidence previously limited to examples. Sensitivity and downstream fine-tuning tests provide further support. The user study has documentation weaknesses—pairwise wording versus a nine-choice interface and undefined uncertainty terms—but the other empirical additions provide a clear substantial overall gain.
